newsitem.title: IRELAND: French film producer's wife murdered in Ireland.
newsitem.headline: French film producer's wife murdered in Ireland.

text.p: Irish police launched a hunt on Tuesday for the killer of the wife of French film producer and critic Daniel Toscan du Plantier, found battered to death on a remote Irish country road.
They said the partially clothed body of Sophie Toscan du Plantier, 38, from Ambrax, near Paris was found close to her holiday home near Schull in County Cork.
"She had severe head injuries," said police Chief Superintendent Noel Smith.
"It would appear that she was bludgeoned to death with some kind of blunt object. It was certainly a most unpleasant scene," he told Irish radio.
Smith said a postmortem was under way and was unable to say whether she had been sexually assaulted.
He described her as a person who kept very much to herself. "We are obviously very anxious to catch the person or persons who did this heinous crime," he added.
Police said Plantier arrived in Cork on Friday evening and had hired a car.
A reporter for Irish radio in Schull said she had planned to stay until December 26 but had later changed her plans and was due to fly back to France on Tuesday.
Her car was still parked outside her cottage on Tuesday and there was no sign of a break-in.
The victim's husband, Daniel Toscan du Plantier, produces and promotes French films and is a familiar figure at the Cannes film festival.
Spokeswomen for his companies Unifrance and Erato Films said he was on holiday in southwestern France and had been informed of the murder.
"Mr Toscan du Plantier just called us. He apparently heard the news today," a spokeswoman for Erato Films told Reuters.
